newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebel web site pays homage to dead rebels.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebel web site pays homage to dead rebels.

text.p: The Internet homepage of Peru's Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movment (MRTA) carried stirring images and slogans on Saturday in tribute to the rebels killed in the raid on the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima.

"Honor to the Martyrs of the Edgar Sanchez Commando!"; "Tupac Amaru Lives!" and "The Struggle Continues!" read the tributes, alongside shots of the rebels inside the residence before Tuesday's military assault to free 72 hostages.

One image showed a rebel clutching his automatic rifle and flashing a victory sign. Another showed MRTA leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini flanked by two guerrillas during an impromptu news conference at the residence on Dec. 31.

The "MRTA Solidarity Page" maintained by Toronto-based anarchist group "Arm The Spirit," had received more than 113,000 "hits" by Saturday, thanks largely to the notoriety the guerrilla group gained from its spectacular Dec. 17 storming of the residence and 126-day standoff with Peru's government.

"Commander Nestor Cerpa Cartolini ... Present!" said another eulogy to the man who led the mission to hold Peruvian, Bolivian and Japanese hostages as bargaining chips in exchange for 450 jailed comrades.
Cerpa's stand ended violently when 140 crack troops burst into the residence through tunnels and rescued all but one of the hostages last Tuesday.
The MRTA used its web page to wage a propaganda war throughout the 18-week hostage drama by publishing statements charging human rights abuses in Peru.

The site also carries interviews with leaders, messages of support from sympathetic leftist groups and mainstream news reports from the hostage crisis and its aftermath. There are links to other MRTA sites in Spanish, German, Italian and Japanese.

The Spanish-language site, "Voz Rebelde" (Rebel Voice), which is run from Germany, also paid homage to the dead guerrillas and warned that their deaths did not signal the end to the movement's revolutionary fight.
"The Tupac Amaru people will continue their fight against the neo-liberal model and the terrorism of the state," it said.
